subject.title: feat(skills): add option to disable ~/.agents/skills scanning for Claude Code coexistence

question: Should OpenClaw add a public source-level opt-out for built-in skill roots such as `agents-skills-personal`, and what exact `skills.load` API should own it?
rationale: The requested fix adds public config surface and changes built-in skill-source behavior; repository policy sets a high bar for new config knobs and requires maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Approve a typed source-disable setting
options.body: Add a narrow default-empty enum/list under `skills.load`, apply it before discovery and watcher registration, and document upgrade-safe defaults.

options.title: Keep current sources and document workarounds
options.body: Close or deprioritize the request if maintainers decide agent allowlists, per-skill disables, and prompt limits are the supported coexistence controls.

options.title: Defer to broader lazy skill routing
options.body: Track this under a larger on-demand skill selection design, accepting that Claude Code coexistence remains noisy until that work lands.

recommendation.title: Approve a typed source-disable setting
recommendation.body: Add a narrow default-empty enum/list under `skills.load`, apply it before discovery and watcher registration, and document upgrade-safe defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: The watcher/source behavior and prior cleanup comments point to this account as the best available routing owner for a skills-loader config decision.
